title: DNV outlines mandatory UK ETS site visit requirements ahead of 2027 deadline
summary: The UK ETS now mandates maritime emissions reporting from July 2026, requiring verified Annual Emissions Reports (AERs) and compulsory site visits by March 2027. DNV advises operators to complete site visits by February 2027, though the allowance for 'virtual visits' with regulatory approval warrants scrutiny for potential oversight gaps. Operators must furnish approved Emissions Monitoring Plans (EMPs) and comprehensive documentation, ensuring robust verification of actual carbon intensity, not just superficial compliance.
content:
The first UK ETS maritime reporting period covers July 1 to December 31, 2026, with Annual Emissions Reports (AERs) required to be verified by March 31, 2027. To avoid delays, DNV recommends completing site visits by the end of February 2027. The classification society has also advised the following:

Physical and virtual site visit requirements

Under the UK ETS, site visits are a mandatory part of the annual verification process. Their location and scope are determined by the verifier’s risk analysis, focusing on how emissions data is monitored, managed and reported.

A site visit does not necessarily require attendance on every vessel or at every company location. DNV’s standard approach is to conduct the visit at the International Safety Management (ISM) Company.

While physical visits are normally expected, virtual visits may be permitted where the verifier determines that they can provide reasonable assurance and the maritime operator obtains regulatory approval.

Applications for virtual visits must be submitted by February 28 of the year following the reporting period, accompanied by relevant information from the verifier, including the risk analysis findings. For the 2026 reporting period, this means February 28, 2027.

Documentation and verification requirements

DNV emphasizes that operators must have an approved Emissions Monitoring Plan (EMP), maintained at company level, identifying the monitoring methodology, vessels under the operator’s responsibility and relevant emissions sources.

Ship-level emissions data is consolidated into a single company-level AER, which must be verified before submission to the regulator.

To support verification, operators should prepare:

An approved Emissions Monitoring Plan (EMP).

The verifier’s risk analysis.

Documentation of data-flow activities and control procedures.

A complete list of vessels covered by the company-level AER.

Regulatory approval for a virtual site visit, where applicable.

The previous year’s verification report, where verification was conducted by another verifier, applicable from the second reporting period.

Early planning to avoid compliance delays

DNV recommends arranging site visits early and, where possible, coordinating them with existing EU MRV, FuelEU Maritime verification activities and relevant ISM company audits to reduce duplication and administrative burdens.

Operators are also encouraged to review their monitoring procedures, prepare supporting evidence and engage with their verifier ahead of the reporting deadline.
